intro: Three people, one lease, and the lowest per-person cost you can get near WashU without sharing a bedroom. The 3 bedroom is how most junior-year groups do it.

Below is every live 3 bedroom on Proximity with its walk time to campus and reviews from students who lived there. One honest warning: group leases live and die on the landlord. Read the reviews before you fall in love with the porch.
directAnswer: 3 bedroom apartments near WashU are mostly houses and flats in Skinker-DeBaliviere, University City, and the blocks around the Delmar Loop. For context, HUD's FY2026 fair market rent for a 3 bedroom is $1,470 in Skinker-DeBaliviere (63112) and $1,750 in University City (63130), whole unit, utilities included.

faqs.q: How much is a 3 bedroom near WashU per person?
faqs.a: Divide the whole-unit rent by three and add utilities if they are separate. As a benchmark, HUD's FY2026 fair market rent for a 3 bedroom is $1,470 in ZIP 63112 and $1,750 in 63130, utilities included, which is a ZIP-wide 40th percentile figure rather than a student-block price. Real rents per listing are shown above.

faqs.q: When do groups need to have a lease signed?
faqs.a: Earlier than you think. Students report private landlords start signing around November for next August, and the well-located 3 bedrooms are the first inventory to disappear because every group of three wants the same ten blocks. Get your group and budget agreed by October and you will have real options.

faqs.q: Joint lease or individual leases: which is better for a group?
faqs.a: A joint lease makes the whole group responsible together, which is simpler but means a flaky housemate is everyone's problem. Individual leases separate your liability but are rarer in this market outside big student buildings. Check which structure each listing uses, and read our lease guide before anyone signs.

faqs.q: What should a group check before signing?
faqs.a: The landlord's reputation above everything: reviews on the listing, how fast maintenance actually happens, and whether the deposit came back for previous tenants. Then the boring stuff that bites groups: subleasing rules for summer, who handles lawn or snow on houses, and exactly which utilities you carry.

benchmarkNote: Rent context on this page cites HUD FY2026 Small Area Fair Market Rents (huduser.gov), whole-unit figures with utilities included. Source: HUD; Source: Zillow Research. Proximity does not publish averages computed from its own listings.
